Medicaid’s core failure isn’t funding—it’s bureaucratic bloat. The program hemorrhages taxpayer dollars through administrative overreach, fraud, and inefficiency. Real reform means slashing redundant layers, auditing every dollar, and redirecting resources to patients—not sustaining a system where 1 in 4 dollars is lost to waste. 

Colorado’s Medicaid budget ballooned 40% since 2020 while outcomes stagnate. That’s not care—it’s a slush fund for bureaucrats. Common sense starts with mandatory clawbacks on misspent funds, capping administrative costs at 5%, and requiring states to match federal dollars. 

Until D.C. stops treating Medicaid as an untouchable jobs program for paper-pushers, taxpayers will keep bankrolling failure.

Verification of legal status before the distribution of Medicaid benefits is essential. 

Medicaid should be protected for eligible Coloradans and not diverted away from those in most need.

This isn’t hypothetical—states like California have exploited loopholes, using Medicaid infrastructure to bankroll care for illegals while veterans and working families wait. The bill forces accountability, requiring HHS to audit states gaming the system and end the backdoor funding of noncitizen benefits. 

Every dollar wasted on this bureaucratic overreach is stolen from programs that serve LEGAL residents. Time to slam the door on this abuse.
